description: 24 real situations taken from Indian court, consumer commission and CIC decisions. Each query is written in plain words from the facts of the decision; the expected documents are the corpus documents that hold the law the decision applied (plus closely related corpus documents that are also correct).

single_domain_queries.query: I paid a hospital about 7.7 lakh rupees for 245 physiotherapy sessions over nine months for neck stiffness. The treatment did not help, they stopped it suddenly and they kept my advance for sessions I never got. Can I get my money back?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Consumer Protection Act, 2019: s.2(11) deficiency, s.2(42) service, s.35 complaint, s.39 relief (refund). Supporting: IMA v. V.P. Shantha (medical services are covered).
expected_primary_documents: Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha, (1995) 6 SCC 651
single_domain_queries.source_case: Rajkanwar Singh Bhangoo v. Cloudnine Hospital (State Consumer Commission)
single_domain_queries.notes: Medical service is a 'service' under CPA; refund of advance for sessions not rendered.

single_domain_queries.query: I bought a OnePlus phone on Flipkart sold as brand new. It hung and drained battery at once, and the service centre says it was activated months before I bought it, so it was a used phone. Flipkart and the seller refuse a refund or replacement. What can I do?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Consumer Protection Act, 2019: s.2(46) unfair contract, s.47(1)(a)(ii); E-Commerce Rules, 2020 (duties of marketplace and seller); Dark Patterns Guidelines, 2023. Supporting: Sale of Goods Act, 1930.
expected_primary_documents: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023
single_domain_queries.source_case: Ashwani Chawla v. Flipkart Internet Pvt. Ltd. (State Consumer Commission)
single_domain_queries.notes: Decision relied on CPA 2(46), 47(1)(a)(ii) and the Dark Patterns Guidelines 2023.

single_domain_queries.query: I was admitted to hospital for eight days with typhoid and a urine infection and paid 68,000 rupees. My health insurer rejected the claim saying hospitalisation was not needed. Where can I complain?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Consumer Protection Act, 2019: s.2(11) deficiency, s.35 complaint. Alternative route: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (r.13 duties, r.14 complaints).
expected_primary_documents: The Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (updated to 18 May 2021)
single_domain_queries.source_case: Star Health & Allied Insurance v. Priya Devi (Delhi State Consumer Commission)
single_domain_queries.notes: Tests whether the Insurance Ombudsman route is found as well as the consumer commission. Outcome of the case was for the insurer; Set 3 only tests the law found.

single_domain_queries.query: We paid a builder about 13 lakh rupees for a flat but never got possession. The builder's man took the refund cheques and never paid us back. Can we get a refund with interest?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Consumer Protection Act, 2019: s.2(11), s.35, s.39 (refund with interest). Supporting: LDA v. M.K. Gupta; Experion Developers v. Sushma Ashok Shiroor; Rohit Chaudhary v. Vipul Ltd.; Jurisdiction Rules, 2021.
expected_primary_documents: Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta, (1994) 1 SCC 243
Experion Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. Sushma Ashok Shiroor, Civil Appeal No. 6044 of 2019, decided 7 April 2022
Rohit Chaudhary v. M/S Vipul Ltd., 2023 INSC 807
The Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021
single_domain_queries.source_case: Narinder Verma v. YPS Developers Pvt. Ltd. (NCDRC)
single_domain_queries.notes: Housing construction is a service (LDA v. M.K. Gupta); refund with interest for non-delivery.

single_domain_queries.query: I ordered a new HP laptop on Amazon for 27,190 rupees and received an old damaged one. I uploaded photos and asked for a return but nobody replied and the return window closed. What are my rights?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Consumer Protection Act, 2019: s.2(10) defect, s.35, s.39 (refund or replacement); E-Commerce Rules, 2020 (returns and refunds). Supporting: Sale of Goods Act, 1930.
single_domain_queries.source_case: Sanjeev Gupta v. Amazon Seller Services Pvt. Ltd. (Haryana State Consumer Commission)
single_domain_queries.notes: Defective / used goods delivered by an e-commerce platform; full refund ordered.

single_domain_queries.query: I ordered a foldable laptop desk online and got a dirty rice bowl instead. The platform refused to replace it saying the return window was over and that it is only an intermediary, not the seller. Is the platform responsible?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Consumer Protection Act, 2019: s.2(7) consumer, s.2(11), s.35; E-Commerce Rules, 2020 (marketplace liability). Related: IT Act, 2000 s.79 (intermediary defence, rejected).
single_domain_queries.source_case: Amazon Seller Services Pvt. Ltd. v. Jaspreet Kaur (Punjab State Consumer Commission)
single_domain_queries.notes: Platform held liable for deficiency despite claiming intermediary status (IT Act s.79).

single_domain_queries.query: I left my ATM card in the machine by mistake. Three days later five withdrawals of 39,000 rupees were made from my account. I told the bank within two days but it refunded only 14,000. Is the bank liable for the rest?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: RBI circular on Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (6 July 2017): zero liability if reported within 3 working days (para 6), limited liability (para 7). Route: RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme or Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
expected_primary_documents: Reserve Bank of India - Customer Protection - Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18, 6 July 2017)
The Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 (with 2022 amendments)
single_domain_queries.source_case: Ramhet v. Punjab & Sind Bank (State Consumer Commission)
single_domain_queries.notes: RBI 2017 zero / limited liability circular (reported within three working days).

single_domain_queries.query: I got a call saying my SMS service would be blocked and an SMS link to click. After I clicked it, 2.6 lakh rupees were taken from my account by net banking. I told the bank at once, but the ombudsman gave back only 33,000. What can I do?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: RBI 6 July 2017 circular (paras 6-7); RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme; Consumer Protection Act, 2019 s.2(11). Reporting: National Cybercrime Reporting Portal.
expected_primary_documents: Reserve Bank of India - Customer Protection - Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18, 6 July 2017)
The Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 (with 2022 amendments)
National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal - Citizen User Manual (reporting cyber crimes other than child sexual abuse material)
User Manual for Reporting Cyber Crime Against Women and Children / Citizen Manual for National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
single_domain_queries.source_case: Hare Ram Singh v. Reserve Bank of India (Delhi High Court)
single_domain_queries.notes: RBI 6 July 2017 circular clauses 6-7; CPA 2(11); ombudsman scheme.

single_domain_queries.query: I am a seafarer. While I was on the ship, 98 online card transactions worth about 12.8 lakh rupees were made from my account. I never shared my PIN and never got any SMS or email alerts. The bank refunded only part. Can I claim compensation?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: IT Act, 2000: s.43, s.43A (failure to protect data), s.46 (adjudicating officer); SPDI Rules, 2011 r.8 (security practices). Related: RBI 6 July 2017 circular.
expected_primary_documents: The Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011
Reserve Bank of India - Customer Protection - Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18, 6 July 2017)
single_domain_queries.source_case: Manvir Singh v. ICICI Bank (appeal under the IT Act, 2000)
single_domain_queries.notes: IT Act 43, 43A, 46 (adjudicating officer) and SPDI Rules rule 8.

single_domain_queries.query: I clicked a link that looked like my bank's eKYC page and entered the OTP I received. 49,997 rupees went out by IMPS. I reported it to the bank and police, but the bank says it was my fault. Do I have any right to a refund?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: RBI 6 July 2017 circular (customer-negligence clause); IT Act, 2000 s.66C (identity theft), s.66D (cheating by personation); BNS, 2023 s.318-319; report on the Cybercrime Portal.
expected_primary_documents: Reserve Bank of India - Customer Protection - Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18, 6 July 2017)
The Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 (with 2022 amendments)
National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal - Citizen User Manual (reporting cyber crimes other than child sexual abuse material)
User Manual for Reporting Cyber Crime Against Women and Children / Citizen Manual for National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
single_domain_queries.source_case: Vikas Mehra v. State Bank of India (Chandigarh State Consumer Commission)
single_domain_queries.notes: Customer shared OTP: customer-negligence clause of the RBI 2017 circular; phishing is IT Act 66C/66D, BNS cheating by personation.

single_domain_queries.query: Someone in my family is posting vulgar messages and my photos with my phone number on WhatsApp and social media, calling me a prostitute. A court already told him to stop. What law covers this and how do I get the posts removed?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: IT Act, 2000 s.67 / s.67A (obscene / sexually explicit material); BNS, 2023 s.75 (sexual harassment), s.79 (insulting modesty), s.356 (defamation); IT Intermediary Rules, 2021 (takedown); Cybercrime Portal.
expected_primary_documents: The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
User Manual for Reporting Cyber Crime Against Women and Children / Citizen Manual for National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal - Citizen User Manual (reporting cyber crimes other than child sexual abuse material)
single_domain_queries.source_case: Keshav Gautam v. State of GNCTD (Delhi High Court)
single_domain_queries.notes: Charged under IT Act 67/67A and IPC 354A/509 (now BNS 75/79); takedown under IT Rules 2021.

single_domain_queries.query: I took a small loan from a mobile loan app and have already repaid more than I borrowed. Their agents keep threatening to send morphed nude photos of me to everyone in my contacts. What can I do?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: IT Act, 2000 s.67A; BNS, 2023 s.308 (extortion), s.351 (criminal intimidation); IT Intermediary Rules, 2021; Cybercrime Portal. Related: DPDP Act, 2023 (misuse of contacts).
expected_primary_documents: The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
User Manual for Reporting Cyber Crime Against Women and Children / Citizen Manual for National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal - Citizen User Manual (reporting cyber crimes other than child sexual abuse material)
The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
single_domain_queries.source_case: Manjunadri Shankarappa v. State of Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Pradesh High Court)
single_domain_queries.notes: Charged under IT Act 67A and IPC 386 / 306 (now BNS 308 extortion, 351 intimidation).

single_domain_queries.query: I rent a small clinic in Delhi for 400 rupees a month. My landlord cut off the electricity and water and removed the bathroom to force me to leave. Can I get the supply restored?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 s.45 (landlord must not cut off an essential supply or service).
single_domain_queries.source_case: M.L. Verma v. Avtar Chand (Delhi Rent Controller)
single_domain_queries.notes: DRC Act s.45: cutting off essential supply or service.

single_domain_queries.query: I run a shop in Tilak Nagar, Delhi on rent. The landlords filed an eviction petition saying their grandson needs the shop to start a fashion boutique. How do I defend this, and is there a time limit?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 s.14(1)(e) (bona fide requirement), s.25B (summary procedure; leave to defend in 15 days). Supporting: Satyawati Sharma; Precision Steel; Sarla Ahuja.
expected_primary_documents: Satyawati Sharma (Dead) by LRs v. Union of India, (2008) 5 SCC 287
Precision Steel & Engineering Works v. Prem Deva Niranjan Deva Tayal, (1982) 3 SCC 270
Sarla Ahuja v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., (1998) 8 SCC 119
single_domain_queries.source_case: H.S. Bajaj v. Satish Chopra (Delhi High Court)
single_domain_queries.notes: Bona fide requirement s.14(1)(e); summary procedure and leave to defend s.25B.

single_domain_queries.query: Our landlord in Delhi filed a civil suit to evict us, saying we sublet part of the premises without his written consent. The rent is under 3,500 a month. Can a civil court even hear this?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 s.14(1)(b) (subletting without written consent), s.16, s.50 (civil court barred).
single_domain_queries.source_case: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries v. Lt. Col. B.M. Singh (Delhi High Court)
single_domain_queries.notes: Subletting ground s.14(1)(b), restriction s.16, civil court bar s.50.

single_domain_queries.query: In my eviction case in Delhi the Rent Controller ordered me to deposit the monthly rent. I deposited one month five days late by mistake. The landlord now wants my defence struck out. Can he do that?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 s.15(1) (order to deposit rent), s.15(7) (striking out the defence).
single_domain_queries.source_case: K.K. Gujral v. Pramod Gupta (Rent Control Tribunal, Delhi)
single_domain_queries.notes: Deposit of rent s.15(1); striking out defence s.15(7).

single_domain_queries.query: My landlord in Delhi filed an eviction petition saying I owe rent, but he never sent me any notice demanding the arrears first. Is his petition valid?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 s.14(1)(a) (arrears of rent; a written demand notice is needed first). Related: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s.106.
single_domain_queries.source_case: Virender v. Mohd. Majid (Delhi District Court)
single_domain_queries.notes: Arrears ground s.14(1)(a) requires a prior demand notice; TPA s.106 notice.

single_domain_queries.query: I have run a boutique from a rented shop in Rajouri Garden, Delhi since 1992 at 872 rupees a month. The landlord says he needs it for his own garment shop because his service station was shut down. The shop is my only livelihood. Can he evict me?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 s.14(1)(e), s.19 (re-letting bar), s.25B. Supporting: Satyawati Sharma; Precision Steel; Sarla Ahuja.
expected_primary_documents: Satyawati Sharma (Dead) by LRs v. Union of India, (2008) 5 SCC 287
Precision Steel & Engineering Works v. Prem Deva Niranjan Deva Tayal, (1982) 3 SCC 270
Sarla Ahuja v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., (1998) 8 SCC 119
single_domain_queries.source_case: Surinder Singh v. Kulbhushan Baluja (Delhi High Court)
single_domain_queries.notes: Bona fide requirement s.14(1)(e); re-letting bar s.19; comparative hardship irrelevant.

single_domain_queries.query: I filed an RTI application with a public sector bank about its MUDRA loans. The information officer never replied and the first appeal officer also did nothing. What can I do, and can the officer be penalised?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: RTI Act, 2005 s.7(1)-(2) (30 days; deemed refusal), s.18 (complaint), s.19 (appeals), s.20 (penalty).
single_domain_queries.source_case: Samir Sardana v. Punjab National Bank (CIC)
single_domain_queries.notes: Deemed refusal s.7(2); complaint s.18; appeal s.19; penalty s.20.

single_domain_queries.query: I asked a bank under RTI for the attendance, leave and transfer records of one of its employees. They refused saying it is personal information held in a fiduciary capacity. Is that allowed?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: RTI Act, 2005 s.8(1)(e) (fiduciary), s.8(1)(j) (personal information), s.11 (third-party procedure). Supporting: Girish Ramchandra Deshpande; CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay.
expected_primary_documents: Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v. Central Information Commissioner, (2013) 1 SCC 212
Central Board of Secondary Education v. Aditya Bandopadhyay, (2011) 8 SCC 497
single_domain_queries.source_case: Sundeep Saggu v. IDBI Bank Ltd (CIC)
single_domain_queries.notes: Exemptions s.8(1)(e), 8(1)(j); third-party procedure s.11.

single_domain_queries.query: I asked a government department under RTI why it changed its appeal rules and asked it to publish the files. It said reasons are not information and the file is too big, and offered only inspection. Is that correct?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: RTI Act, 2005 s.2(f) (what counts as information), s.4 (proactive disclosure), s.7(9) (disproportionate diversion). Supporting: CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay.
expected_primary_documents: Central Board of Secondary Education v. Aditya Bandopadhyay, (2011) 8 SCC 497
single_domain_queries.source_case: Gita Dewan Verma v. Department of Personnel & Training (CIC)
single_domain_queries.notes: Definition of information s.2(f); proactive disclosure s.4; disproportionate diversion s.7(9).

single_domain_queries.query: My RTI application to the municipal corporation was passed from one zone office to another, and I got the information five months later with an irrelevant answer to one question. Can I get compensation or a penalty?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: RTI Act, 2005 s.6(3) (transfer within 5 days), s.7 (time limit), s.19(8)(b) (compensation), s.20 (penalty).
single_domain_queries.source_case: Dr. Pradeep Dutta v. MCD, GNCT Delhi (CIC)
single_domain_queries.notes: Transfer s.6(3); time limit s.7; compensation s.19(8)(b); penalty s.20.

single_domain_queries.query: I need my estranged husband's income details from his tax returns for my maintenance case. Can I get them through RTI? He objects that it is his private information.
single_domain_queries.expected_law: RTI Act, 2005 s.8(1)(j) (personal information), s.11 (third-party notice). Supporting: Girish Ramchandra Deshpande.
expected_primary_documents: Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v. Central Information Commissioner, (2013) 1 SCC 212
single_domain_queries.source_case: Mamta v. Chief Commissioner of Income Tax (CIC)
single_domain_queries.notes: Personal information s.8(1)(j); third-party notice s.11; Girish Ramchandra Deshpande.

single_domain_queries.query: I filed an RTI application without paying the fee because I am below the poverty line, but I did not attach any proof. The officer did not give the information. Do I have to pay the fee?
single_domain_queries.expected_law: RTI Act, 2005 s.6(1) (fee), s.7(5) (no fee for below-poverty-line applicants, with proof); RTI Rules, 2012 (fees).
single_domain_queries.source_case: Srikanth Sreedhar v. National Institute of Technology, Warangal (CIC)
single_domain_queries.notes: Fee s.6(1); BPL exemption proviso to s.7(5); fee under RTI Rules 2012.
